The Happy Days of Youth

Here’s a version inspired by Frankie Gavin’s “flashy” flute playing.

K: Gmaj
efed ~B3A|GABG AGEF|~G3B dg~g2|dBAd BG~G2|
~e3d BdBA|G2BG AGEF|~G3B dgge|dBAd BG~G2||
faag fedf|edef ~g3f|eB~B2 gfed|BAGA BA~A2|
f2ag fedf|edef ~g3a|bgaf gfed|egfa ~g3f||

I believe this is simpler and easier on the flute, but still as effective as other versions. There’s lots of room for variation and ornamentation though.

↳ Posted by slainte on May 15th, 2007.

An old tune

This tune appears, under the title The Happy Days of Youth, in O‘Neill’s ’Music of Ireland’. Does anyone know how John McKenna’s name came to be associated with it?

↳ Posted by rwwt on April 8th, 2011.

Because he recorded it early on in the 78 era, after Colonel Roger’s Favourite, and the set is still very often played together.

↳ Posted by Nico on April 8th, 2011.

Setting #5: Liam Kelly

plays “Thos Byrne’s” on the first Dervish album (on an E whistle though).
https://thesession.org/recordings/394
… followed by “The Man Of Aran”…
https://thesession.org/tunes/973#setting14170

I’ve notated the breath-rests only because he always takes a breath at the very same places, so I couldn’t compensate this by mixing up his takes through the tune.

↳ Posted by sebastian the m3g4p0p on August 11th, 2013.
